holidays.name: Be a Dork Day
holidays.description: A day to let your inner goofball loose. Wear the mismatched socks, snort when you laugh, and break out the dance moves nobody asked for. Today, being a dork is a badge of honor.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on quirky-holiday calendars as a reminder not to take yourself too seriously.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dork' first appeared in American slang in the 1960s. Its exact roots are debated, and it has since gone from insult to something people wear proudly.

holidays.name: Give Something Away Day
holidays.description: A day for clearing out the closet and sharing the wealth. Hand over a book, a spare plant, or a bag of extra garden zucchini. Giving is the whole point, and no one is keeping score.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to pass along things they no longer need to someone who will enjoy them.
holidays.funFact: Some cultures practice gift-giving traditions built around generosity rather than getting something back. The potlatch ceremonies of Pacific Northwest Indigenous peoples are a well-known example.

holidays.name: Gummi Worm Day
holidays.description: A salute to the wiggly, sugar-dusted candy that has been dangled above open mouths since childhood. Stretch one out, bite off the head, or dig into a whole squirming pile.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and candy lovers celebrate it every July 15.
holidays.funFact: Gummy candy traces back to Germany in the 1920s, when Hans Riegel created gummy bears. Gummy worms came later as a squishier cousin.
